segmenti.tekst: [Arabic recitation]

Nahmaduhu ta'ala wa nasta'inuhu wa nastaghfiruhu wa na'udhu billahi min shururi anfusina wa min sayyi'ati a'malina. Man yahdihillahu fala mudilla lah, wa man yudlilhu fala hadiya lah. Wa ashhadu an la ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lah, wa ashhadu anna sayyidana wa nabiyyana Muhammadan 'abduhu wa habibuhu wa rasuluh. Arsalahullahu tabaraka wa ta'ala bil-huda wa dini al-haqqi li yuzhirahu 'ala ad-dini kullihi wa law kariha al-kafirun. Fa salawatu Rabbi

wa salamuhu 'alayhi wa 'ala alihi wa sahbihi wa man sara 'ala nahjihi waqtafa atharahu ila yawm id-din. Ridwanullahi ta'ala 'alayna wa 'alayhim ajma'in. Thumma amma ba'd. Respected brothers, esteemed believers, esteemed… Allah, Allah is the Creator of everything.
Everything besides Him is created. But His most important creation among those vast and numerous worlds is man. Man is the central creation of Allah.

Man is Allah's most important creation. The Exalted Allah honors and esteems man the most, values him, and gives him dignity. Man is Allah's most privileged creation, man is Allah's most honored creation. Allah has subjected everything to man; everything that is in the heavens and on the Earth He has subjected to man. And that should awaken in us pride,

dignity and happiness, because the Perfect, Self-Sufficient, All-Knowing, Wise Creator esteems and honors you, values you, distinguishes you. And that is why our focus and our activity, we people, creatures, should be precisely to subject everything to man, so that everything we do serves the liberation of man, the esteem of man and the service of man.

Because Allah, jalla wa 'ala (majestic and exalted is He), has subjected the angels to man. The angels serve man, my brothers. The sinless angels, who are in the heavens, who have never committed a sin – not only have they not, but they cannot – yet He has subjected them to man. And that is why everything we build – cities, neighborhoods, associations, institutions, companies, states – everything should serve man. It is not an end in itself; rather, it is made and organized to serve

man and to be at his service, to be subjected to us, because we carry what is most valuable, and that is the word of Allah, that is the truth, that is the shahadah (testimony of faith), that is Allah's revelation, Allah's Shari'ah. That is the most valuable of all. That is why we are so valuable, because we have taken on the most important role, the most important message and the most important task.

Today this world has indeed developed technologically, materially and in terms of civilization. Everything sparkles with light, with decorations, with advertisements, with cleanliness and with order. Almost like a fairy tale, perfection.
But little of it serves man. Very often they make all of it in order to trample man, humiliate him, enslave him, bring him down. But Islam does not want that. Islam wants freedom for man, dignity.

Even the state that the Messenger of Allah, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam (peace be upon him), built, as the most important, most just, best institution, was not an end in itself; rather, it served man and tawhid (the oneness of Allah), the truth that man carried.

In this spirit and light we should raise our children and our youth, brothers. And to the extent that we succeed in having as many such individuals as possible – individuals who understand these things and spread this conviction and these meanings in society and the community – it will be better for everyone.
And it has always been individuals who initiated change in society. Allah's messengers. How did Allah send Allah's messengers? Did He send them by the tens, or by the hundreds, or by the thousands?

No, He sends one man at a time. But a man of quality, who changes the whole world. And then the Messenger of Allah, alayhis-salam, as the best Messenger, also showed us the focus on man, raising people of quality, and they will make and create everything else that everyone needs.

The Messenger of Allah polished, educated and raised one man at a time. And then he sent to Medina the young man Mus'ab ibn Umayr. A young man, 17–18 years old, around 20, he was no older. But he was a man who [unclear], who had a clear mind, clear thought.

A free man, and then he freed others. Within a year, faith had entered every house in Medina, freedom had entered, revelation, truth – Mus'ab ibn Umayr. Yemen, a huge region, today it is a state, but it is a place known since ancient times, for thousands of years, ancient Yemen.
And to that people the Messenger of Allah sends how many men? One. Mu'adh ibn Jabal. And then Abu Musa al-Ash'ari as well. Well, an individual is not [unclear].

Khalid ibn al-Walid, when he had finished his affairs with the apostates, set out toward Persia. And he asked… exhausted soldiers, by Allah, a small number. And he asked the caliph Abu Bakr: “Send me support, send me reinforcements.”

And the letter reached Abu Bakr and he said: “I will send you reinforcements.” And he sent him one man. One man! Ancient Persia, an empire, people! At that level it was fiercer than these two well-known empires that rule the world today.

He came to Khalid and said: “I am your support from Abu Bakr. Abu Bakr sent me.” And then, when they asked Abu Bakr, he said: “The voice of al-Qa'qa' ibn Amr among a people and in battle is better than a thousand other soldiers. And a group among whom is al-Qa'qa' ibn Amr will not be defeated.”

Quality, my brothers. Quality. Quality: an educated man, a free man, an individual, learned, who drank from the springs of the Qur'an and the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, for whom the universe is his homeland.

There are no boundaries; the only boundaries are the rulings of Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala (glorified and exalted is He). And very often one hears a saying of, you know, ambitious people; they say: “For us the sky is the limit,” as if, they take pride in it.

For us the first heaven is not the limit, that is very close. We pass through all the heavens, we go up to the seventh heaven, we go to Firdaws, to the Throne and the Lord of the Throne, subhanahu wa ta'ala. Well, those are the ambitions of the believers and the mu'mins, my dear brothers. And that is why we, the people of the Sandžak, are a hardworking people, a capable people, especially the inhabitants of this capital of the Sandžak, the city of Novi Pazar.
They know how to make good investments, and you know how to make good investments, but know that the most important investment is investing in your children and in our children and in our youth.

And in your houses great people are being born and have been born, in sha Allah. Look at your son and daughter as a great person, a great human being. Treat him that way, respect him, esteem him. And Allah [unclear] will not betray your hope that, in sha Allah, he will be at the head not only of your household and clan, but much wider, and in khayr and in goodness,

in commanding good and forbidding evil, in the mission of spreading ethics, morality, justice, truth, what man needs most – spirituality. Spirituality! This humanity groans from a disease called materialism and hedonism. Everything revolves around: what will I eat, what will I drink, where will I go, where will I relax. But where are our souls, brothers? Souls have died, even though people still walk around. And the soul is the foundation, it is the soul

that needs real energy and needs real treatment, and food only as it were, as we say, to help your body serve the soul and serve spirituality and what is most exalted and most valuable. This land called the Sandžak is an incredible land. It is a seed for great things. It never had protection, this material protection, physical protection – not from anyone – but Allah gave…

It has always given birth to sons and daughters. It gave birth to Mehmed Šemsikadić, the mufti of Pljevlja; it gave birth to many sons: Atif-efendi, the late mufti, [unclear] efendi. And do not say: “Those people will never come again.” Never say that. No, in your houses such people are being born, and better than them, in sha Allah, in sha Allahu ta'ala. And they will be born, and there will be, in sha Allah, an even better situation, an even better environment for this area and for the whole region and the peoples who live here in this land. We are a mercy, we are

a blessing, we are bearers of light, and that is what obliges us to rise to the task and, of course, to build institutions and to strengthen them. But institutions are strong only as much as they have people of quality, and as much as they serve man on the path of a sacred and honorable mission.

May Allah protect you. May Allah bless you. May Allah help you to remain steadfast on the right path until the end, in sha Allahu ta'ala. That we may string together many more victories for Islam and for the Muslims, and that we may die with the shahadah, and that our Lord may then be pleased with us. Amin.

Ya Rabb al-alamin. Barakallahu li wa lakum fil-Qur'an al-'azim, وَنَفَعَنِي وَإِيَّاكُمْ بِمَا فِيهِ مِنَ الْآيَاتِ وَالذِّكْرِ الْحَكِيمِ، أَقُولُ مَا تَسْمَعُونَ وَأَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ الْعَظِيمَ لِي وَلَكُمْ فَاسْتَغْفِرُوهُ إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْغَفُورُ الرَّحِيمُ.
